DRAFT · for the Chief of Staff · not sent 
From: Jonathan Paul Zschoche, attorney-in-fact of Patricia Keesey Zschoche 
To: Atty. Bonifacio T. Barandon, Jr. 
Date: ____ October 2026 
Re: Civil Case No. 26-360, where we are after 14 October

Atty. Barandon,

Thank you for Wednesday. I wanted to put down in one page where I think we are, and ask for one thing.

**What happened.** I gave my direct testimony. Atty. Ramos did not fight it. His cross went to one point: that I was not present for anything before 2025, so what I know about the years before comes from documents and from my mother. I agree that is where he will build his defense.

**What that means.** Our case does not depend on me. It rests on the written limit in paragraph 7 of the 1992 power of attorney: Cesar could sell only to people holding Llamanzares contracts or who had paid Llamanzares, and only after consulting the owners. Mrs. Balane was a renter. Her own Answer says so. The power is on Exhibit E, the 1996 annotation is on Exhibit B, the deed is Exhibit H, and the revocation and the 2020 notice are Exhibits F and G. Those are already marked. Nothing we need to win is left to prove through me.

**What I propose for the next weeks.**

- Nothing new is filed before 4 November, except possibly a short motion asking the Court to resolve our April summary judgment motion, which I will send you separately. I am quietly obtaining certified copies we may need later.

- Mrs. King and Shirley De Leon testify on 4 and 11 November, each on her affidavit as filed. Which of the two goes first is your call; I lean to Shirley De Leon first.

- My mother testifies later, on rebuttal, by videoconference from California. I will send you a separate short note on that with her draft affidavit, so you can tell me what the rules require.

- I will add nothing on the stand if I am recalled.

**What I need from you this week:** thirty minutes, in your office or by phone, before 24 October, to go through two decisions only: my mother's testimony, and what we offer on 9 December. Please tell me which day suits you.

And please tell me which of the two, Mrs. King or Shirley De Leon, you want on 4 November, so I can tell them the date. One more small thing: the notarial stamp on the January affidavits reads "valid until 12/31/2025"; please send me the 2026 commission number so I can correct my file.

With respect, 
Jonathan Paul Zschoche
